newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - API data seen showing balanced supplies.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - API data seen showing balanced supplies.

text.p: The American Petroleum Institute's (API) oil inventory report Tuesday is expected by traders to show minor draws in both refined product and crude stocks, though the data is seen reflecting a balanced supply and demand picture overall, dealers and analysts said.

"We are in a holding pattern in terms of supply and demand. Asia seems to have taken some of the excess crude, but we also have a enough crude for refineries in the near term," said Pat Hughes, analyst with Chevron Corp in California.
Trader estimates for crude stocks ranged from a build of three million to a draw of two million barrels.
Traders' expectations yielded a consensus estimate of crude stocks falling one million barrels in the data that reflects the week ended April 25.
"One million up or one million down is not going to change the fundamental crude (supply and demand) picture which for now is balanced," said a New York crude dealer.
Traders noted increased crude demand from Asia and the Mediterranean has stemmed, to some extent, what was a steady stream of imports to the United States from the North Sea and West Africa.

"The rationale behind the crude draw is a fall off in imports. We have also had crude builds for the last several weeks, so a crude draw would be be a regression to the mean in a manner of speaking," said William Brown, president of trading firm W.H. Brown & Co in New York.

Gasoline stocks were seen steady, for the most part, to dropping up to 1.5 million barrels. Implied demand was expected to ease from the lofty level that last week's data yielded of 8.3 million barrels per day (bpd). Imports, as in crude, were expected to drop.

One New York dealer expected gasoline stocks to rise by two million barrels due to a continuing high production rate. Last week's data, which reflected the week ended April 18, said gasoline production was 7.7 million bpd.
"Refiners want to take advantage of what have been good margins," said the dealer. The gasoline-to-crude crack spread has averaged above $6.00 a barrel throughout April.
Still, dealers expect refinery runs to have slackened from a high 93.5 percent.
Distillate stocks, which include heating oil and diesel, were seen dropping one to 1.5 million barrels.

To prepare for the summer driving season, refiners have shifted away from distillate output to make gasoline. But, heating oil demand continues firm due to unseasonably cold weather in the U.S. Northeast, dealers said.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
